blocks.section: Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act
blocks.text:
SB 54

SB 54 establishes a new extended producer responsibility (EPR) program to manage packaging and single-use plastic food service ware products across every sector of the economy.

EPR gives primary responsibility for managing products after their useful life to producers, who can design and market products to be more easily reused or recycled.

- On November 2, 2026, CalRecycle published the Update to the Source Reduction Baseline Report along with the Source Reduction Guidance webpage.
- On October 13, 2026, CalRecycle received Circular Action Alliance’s producer responsibility plan for how producers will meet the law’s requirements. CalRecycle has 75 days to review the plan for compliance under 14 CCR 18980.6.1(b)(2).
- CalRecycle published the Local Jurisdiction and Recycling Service Provider Guidance webpage for local jurisdictions and recycling service providers seeking guidance on compliance and extensions or exemptions from collection requirements under Public Resources Code section 42060.5.
- CalRecycle posted *de minimis* exclusion on the new Exclusion for Certain *De Minimis* Components database webpage, which helps interested parties understand which specific components do not have reporting or fee obligations.
- CalRecycle has published updated information regarding the collection and sortation of non-CRV cartons (both gable-top and aseptic). This updated information will inform the next update to the Covered Material Categories List, which will be published by January 1, 2027.
- **Circular Action Alliance** has been approved to serve as the first Producer Responsibility Organization. (PRC 42061.5)

Packaging makes up over 50% of what we dump in California landfills by volume. We must reduce packaging waste and ensure it is recycled to meet our state’s recycling and climate goals.

On June 30, 2022, Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 54 (Allen, 2022) into law to address the impacts of single-use packaging and plastic food service ware. This landmark packaging law requires that by 2032, we:

- Packaging
- Plastic food service ware
